title: Gambits
line: A pawn given up early can buy time, open lines and the center.

steps.text: A gambit gives up a pawn, or more, early. In return the pieces come out faster and get open lines.
Push the pawn in front of your king two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares as well.
Offer a second pawn: move the pawn on c2 one square.
Do not take back. Offer a third pawn and bring the bishop out, aimed at f7.

also.b1c3: Taking back is also sound. This lesson offers another pawn.

steps.after: Engines rate this gambit as too much: with care Black stays better, and masters seldom play it.

steps.text: Take back with the other bishop. Now both bishops aim at the king side.
steps.after: The Danish Gambit: two pawns for open lines. Here Black brings its bishop out, a rare slip that leaves g7 to your bishop.

steps.text: That slip leaves g7 unguarded. Take the pawn: your bishop then attacks the rook in the corner.
steps.after: The rook has no safe square. The open line you gave two pawns for wins it.

summary: A gambit pays a pawn for time and open lines. It works when the pieces use them before the other side catches up.
